verdict: Berkshire's operating earnings rose 18% to $11.3B on a clean insurance quarter — and a $1.6B paper loss on its stock portfolio held headline profit to $10.1B, still more than double a year ago.

kpis.label: Operating earnings
kpis.note: +18% YoY — the number Buffett says matters

kpis.label: Insurance underwriting
kpis.note: +29% YoY, after tax — no major storms

segments.name: Insurance premiums earned
segments.note: Premiums from GEICO, reinsurance and primary insurance — barely up on a year ago.

segments.note: The biggest bucket: everything the manufacturing, service and retailing businesses sell — now including OxyChem, the chemical business Berkshire bought in January.

otherDetail: Investment losses of $1,605M — mostly paper losses on Berkshire's stock portfolio — plus $176M of equity-method earnings, less $73M attributable to noncontrolling interests.
footerNote: Berkshire has no single gross-profit line: costs are split following the 10-Q's own structure.
follow100Note: The pattern flipped from last quarter: the stock portfolio subtracted $1.71 of every $100 instead of adding to it, so the operating businesses earned the whole $10.79 Berkshire kept — and covered the portfolio's paper loss too. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Operating earnings up 18%
takeaways.text: The businesses themselves earned $11.3B after tax, up from $9.6B — insurance underwriting jumped to $1.7B with no significant catastrophe losses, versus $860M of storm losses a year ago.

takeaways.title: A paper loss on the stock pile
takeaways.text: Investment losses of $1.6B were mostly unrealized: the value of stocks Berkshire still holds fell $3.3B, partly offset by $1.7B of gains on stocks sold during the quarter ($24.1B of sales).

takeaways.title: OxyChem joins the family
takeaways.text: Berkshire closed its roughly $9.5B purchase of Occidental's chemical business on January 2, 2026 — and the cash pile at its insurance and other businesses still stood at $373.5B at quarter-end.

oneTimers: Investment losses are mostly paper losses. Of the $1,605M pre-tax investment losses, $3,291M was a fall in unrealized gains on stocks Berkshire still holds, partly offset by $1,652M of gains on stocks sold. Next quarter the unrealized part can just as easily reverse.
No repeat of last year's catastrophe hit: the first quarter of 2025 carried about $860M of after-tax losses from significant catastrophe events; this quarter had none.
